newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb mid-session on bottom-fishing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb mid-session on bottom-fishing.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from a slow start to broach the pyschological 4,500-point barrier in late morning trade on Tuesday due to what dealers said was light bargain-hunting.
"Buyers retreated yesterday and when they saw little selling, they stepped back in. The market is firm and buying is mixed. Telmex is helping, but not much," a desk trader said.
"I feel they are bottom-fishing after yesterday's profit-taking," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 42.67 points, or 0.97 percent, at 4,500.64.
"Locals seem to be very liquid, foreigners are just switching positions. Dealing is slow, on the whole they're buying, but things are quiet," another floor trader said.

"Right now, with all that is happening this week and at the weekend, it is best to stay where you are," he added, referring to the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2, and Mexican mid-term elections on July 6.
Trading volume was was slower than for many recent sessions at 34.1 million shares traded.
Market heavyweight Telmex was up 12 centavos to 19.14 pesos, from an early dip to 18.94 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 48 to 18 out of a total of 90 stocks traded.
Dealers had forecast hikes of up to 300 basis points in Cetes rates on Monday. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile up 19/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
Mexico will hold elections on July 6 to renew the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, six state governors and a historic direct poll for Mexico City mayor.
"The market is very strong, secondary interst rates have fallen sharply, a lot of foreigners are in the market again. They seem to be buying ahead of smooth elections," a desk trader said.
Volume of 111.7 million shares evidenced vigourous trading by both domestic and foreign investors.
"We are also seeing certain repositioning ahead of expected good second quarter numbers in Ara, Hogar some retailers and Tamsa," Schonander added.
Retailer Cifra gained 20 centavos to 15.00 pesos in brisk dealing. Steelmaker Tamsa rose 6.70 pesos to 152.50 pesos.
Construction firm Consorcio Ara gained 55 centavos to 28.50 pesos, while fellow builder Consorcio Hogar rose 46 centavos to 11.80 pesos.
